name: Svelte
summary: A compiler-oriented UI framework that transforms component files into imperative update code, with component boundaries and DOM operations largely established during compilation.

features.name: Component as source program
features.description: Svelte treats a component file as a source unit containing script, markup, and style regions that the compiler parses into a component representation.
benefits: Keeps component structure close to ordinary HTML, CSS, and JavaScript
Gives the compiler a complete unit for static analysis
costs: Component semantics depend on compiler rules
Tooling must understand the component-file format

features.name: Compile-time DOM update generation
features.description: The compiler lowers component markup and expressions into DOM creation and update instructions, moving much of the rendering work from runtime tree comparison into generated component code.
benefits: Can produce focused update operations for known dependencies
Reduces the need for a general runtime virtual-DOM diff
costs: Build output is coupled to compiler behavior
Dynamic patterns can limit static optimization

features.name: Reactive declaration updates
features.description: Svelte's compiler recognizes reactive declarations and assignments in component code and emits invalidation/update paths that keep dependent markup synchronized.
benefits: Uses ordinary-looking assignment syntax for local updates
Makes dependency relationships available during compilation
costs: Dependency analysis has syntax and aliasing limits
Generated invalidation order becomes part of observable behavior

mathematical_views.question: How do script, markup, and style regions map to generated component artifacts and runtime operations?
assumptions: A component file is a finite source graph
Compiler passes preserve declared component dependencies
Bundler and module-linking behavior are abstracted

mathematical_views.question: Which generated update operations are enabled when a component variable or reactive expression changes?
assumptions: Assignments and expressions define dependency edges
The compiler can conservatively identify relevant reads
DOM mutation ordering is represented but browser layout is abstracted

mathematical_views.question: Which rendering costs can be shifted from component execution to compilation without changing the component's observable update behavior?
assumptions: Generated code is semantically equivalent for supported syntax
Dynamic evaluation and external state are modeled as residual runtime work

costs: Compiler-aware syntax and tooling are required
Build pipeline and generated output become central constraints
Static dependency analysis can be sensitive to code shape
